newsitem.title: CHINA: HK property stocks fall on land supply plans.
newsitem.headline: HK property stocks fall on land supply plans.

text.p: Shares in Hong Kong property developers fell sharply on Wednesday after the government said it would boost land supply dramatically over coming years.
The Hang Seng properties sub-index was down 604 points, or 2.43 percent, at 24,216 in early trade, weighing on the blue chip Hang Seng Index which eased 21 points, or 0.14 percent, to 15,465.
"It's a kneejerk reaction to the announcement vis-a-vis the increase in land supply," said James Osborn, sales director at ING Barings.

Secretary for Planning, Environment and Development Bowen Leung said on Tuesday that the government would increase land supply by 140 percent over the next five years compared with the previous five years.
Shares in Cheung Kong fell HK$1.50 to HK$75.25, Henderson Land was off HK$1.75 at HK$67.00 and Sun Hung Kai Properties fell HK$2.00 to HK$88.75.
"Property is still under pressure but I believe in the afternoon it will be steadier," said Peter Lui, in institutional sales at NAVA SC Securities.
He said investors had already discounted an increase in land supply.
"Some people are suggesting that physical property prices might come down but it is too early to say if we will see an actual pullback in prices," said Osborn.
